title: Accounts Assistant
description:

title: Accounts Assistant
description:
Could your eye for detail help strengthen financial controls and keep month-end running smoothly as an Accounts Assistant?

The Organisation

Join a growing Edinburgh-based company that values accuracy, integrity and strong working relationships. You will work in a supportive finance team with opportunities to develop your skills and progress your career.
- Support a growing organisation with a strong focus on long-term relationships.

The Role

As an Accounts Assistant, you will support accurate accounts payable and month-end processes. Your work will help the team produce reliable financial information and maintain effective controls.
- Process supplier invoices and employee expense claims, checking coding and approvals.
- Maintain supplier records and support supplier onboarding and amendments.
- Prepare payment runs, ledger allocations and related reconciliations.
- Post journals, accruals and other month-end accounting adjustments.
- Complete balance sheet, ledger and suspense account reconciliations.
- Respond to supplier and colleague queries and support finance projects.

The Ideal Candidate

You will be organised, analytical and confident working to deadlines. This role suits someone who enjoys solving problems, working with detail and collaborating across a business.

Mandatory
- Demonstrate previous experience in finance, accounts payable or financial control.
- Show experience supporting month-end activities and meeting reporting deadlines.
- Apply strong attention to detail, communication and problem-solving skills.

Preferred
- Understand invoice processing, payment workflows, journals and reconciliations.
- Use Excel confidently, with experience of Power Query, Copilot or Power BI.
- Show interest in working towards a relevant professional accounting qualification.

On Offer

The organisation supports hybrid working and will consider flexible working requests. The successful candidate will receive support with professional development and gain exposure to wider finance activity.
- Develop your career within a growing Edinburgh-based company.
- Work closely with colleagues across finance and the wider organisation.
- Gain exposure to process improvement, automation and business change.
- Receive support towards a relevant professional accounting qualification.
- Discuss flexible working arrangements during the recruitment process.

title: Credit Control
description:
We are recruiting on behalf of a long-established manufacturing company based in Edinburgh, supplying trade customers across Scotland and the wider UK. Our client is looking for an experienced Credit Controller to manage its debtor ledger and strengthen its credit processes.

This is a stable, varied role in a business where people tend to stay - perfect for someone who wants security, routine and a team that feels like family.

Location: Edinburgh

Employment: Permanent, full-time

The Role
- Managing the full credit control cycle for a ledger of trade customers.
- Chasing payments by phone and email, building strong relationships with regular accounts.
- Setting up new customer accounts, running credit checks and agreeing terms.
- Allocating payments and resolving invoice and pricing queries.
- Preparing aged debt reports and presenting them at monthly finance meetings.
- Recommending accounts for stop supply or legal action where necessary.
- Working closely with sales and customer service teams to resolve disputes.

A Typical Day

You will start by checking the bank statement and allocating receipts, then move on to your call list for the day. Much of the role is relationship-based - you will know your regular customers by name and understand their payment cycles. Afternoons often involve resolving queries, updating the ledger and preparing reports. It is steady, satisfying work where accuracy and consistency really count.

What We Are Looking For
- Solid experience in credit control, ideally in a trade, manufacturing or distribution environment.
- A firm but friendly approach to collections.
- Good working knowledge of accounting packages and Excel.
- Strong organisational skills and the ability to prioritise a busy workload.
- A team player who communicates well across departments.
- CICM qualification or part-qualification is an advantage but not essential.

What You Can Expect
- A permanent, full-time position with a secure, long-established employer.
- 28 days' paid annual leave including bank holidays.
- Early finish on Fridays.
- Free on-site parking and good public transport links.
- A supportive, down-to-earth team culture.

If you want a credit control role where you can settle in and make the ledger your own, apply through Consula today.
